record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: What breakthrough is required to obtain a successful, quantitatively reliable first-principles approach to finite-density baryonic matter from QCD? In particular, since existing phenomenological descriptions have substantial model dependence and there is currently no established successful method for finite-density baryonic matter, what new conceptual or computational development would allow QCD itself to describe such matter quantitatively?

evidence.quote: At this moment, there is no successful approach to the study of finite-density baryonic matter. To understand the origin of baryonic matter, a breakthrough is needed.
Very unfortunately, there is no established way to solve finite-density QCD.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the Euclidean lattice path integral at nonzero baryon chemical potential μ has a complex action: the fermion determinant det M(μ) satisfies [det M(μ)]* = det M(−μ*), so for real μ ≠ 0 the integrand of the partition function

  Z(μ) = ∫ DU e^{−S_g[U]} det M(U,μ)

is not real-positive. This obstructs standard importance-sampling Monte Carlo and is known as the sign problem of finite-density lattice QCD. Existing techniques (reweighting, Taylor expansion in μ/T, imaginary-μ analytic continuation, complex Langevin dynamics, Lefschetz thimble methods, density-of-states approaches, tensor-network and quantum-computing approaches) are restricted to small μ/T, suffer from uncontrolled systematic errors, fail to converge correctly in physically relevant regimes, or are not yet scalable to four-dimensional QCD with physical quark masses.

Problem. Provide a quantitatively reliable, first-principles method for evaluating expectation values

  ⟨O⟩ = (1/Z(μ)) ∫ DU e^{−S_g[U]} det M(U,μ) O[U]

in lattice QCD with Nf = 2+1 flavors at physical quark masses for baryon chemical potentials μ_B in the cold, dense regime (T ≪ μ_B, with μ_B of order the nucleon mass), with controlled and systematically improvable errors, sufficient to compute the equation of state and phase structure of finite-density baryonic matter directly from QCD. Equivalently, exhibit a conceptual or computational development that overcomes the finite-density sign problem in this regime and demonstrate its quantitative reliability against known benchmarks.
artifact.status_search_result: The finite-density QCD sign problem remains an open problem. Recent reviews and ongoing contributions to the Lattice 2025 symposium continue to discuss complex Langevin, Lefschetz thimble, density-of-states, machine-learning, and quantum-computing approaches, but none has been established as a quantitatively reliable first-principles method for cold, dense baryonic matter at physical quark masses.

status_evidence.title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: Current status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Current status and open problems in finite-density lattice QCD; no established successful method for finite-density baryonic matter.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as open with no established solution.

status_evidence.title: Lattice 2025 Contribution List
status_evidence.snippet: Numerous 2025 contributions still address complex Langevin, thimbles, density-of-states, and ML approaches to the sign problem.
status_evidence.claim: The sign problem is still actively studied as of 2025 with no decisive breakthrough.

status_evidence.title: Sign problem in lattice QCD (nLab)
status_evidence.snippet: Importance-sampling fails for QCD at finite baryon density; multiple partial approaches exist but none fully solves the problem.
